# **What Is Great Content?**

Great content, above all else, is immensely valuable to the reader. No matter the words, formatting, and media used to get there, the reader should have a clear takeaway, and something tactical they can use for their own work. Here is some great content, and examples of takeaways for you to understand:

[**Post**](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nick-abraham_coldemail-coldemailtips-leadgeneration-activity-7149021881004699649-PUTk?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)

**Takeaway:** Template for reader to use.

**Great because:** The reader can copy the template and get the exact benefit they want/need.

[**Post**](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/elirubel_agency-owners-dont-talk-about-this-on-linkedin-activity-7275532870000001024-deNH?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) 

**Takeaway:** Agency owners (the ICP) get to know exactly how much money they should be making.

**Great because:** It gives the reader (targeted to agency owners), clear, *non-obvious* knowledge they likely didn’t have before. Note that this works only because Eli, the account, has the authority to speak on agency margins. More on that later.

[**Post**](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/retentionadam_in-2024-i-grew-rb2b-from-0-4m-in-40-weeks-activity-7278115432052498432-JQa-?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)

**Takeaway:** You will learn the mistakes Adam made while trying to get to $4M ARR.

**Great because:** Based on the hook alone, the reader (who also wants to grow their business to $4M ARR) will clearly be shown the mistakes to avoid in doing so.

You can access our Swipe File of great LinkedIn posts [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CzxGUYd8WRwc9s4VnRWekkwLd2I7MZ0-2rt4CLXDCmI/edit?tab=t.0). You’re expected to read through each one. Additionally, another agency in our space published an amazing guide on great content [here.](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CzxGUYd8WRwc9s4VnRWekkwLd2I7MZ0-2rt4CLXDCmI/edit?tab=t.0) You’re expected to read this in its entirety.

# **How Can You Tell When Content Is Great?**

Aside from strong social metrics, the way to self-evaluate if your content is great can be summed up into a checklist. 

- [ ] Does this post sound like a human wrote it? (i.e. is it free of all jargon, and other AI-generated copy?)  
- [ ] Does it minimize words that are longer than 2 syllables in length?  
- [ ] Is it free of all grammar errors?  
- [ ] Read the post out loud – does it flow the same way a human would speak?  
        
- [ ] After reading the whole post, is there something clear and tactical the reader can take away?  
- [ ] Does the hook give the reader **no choice** but to click “see more” on LinkedIn?  
- [ ] Is the post formatted so that it’s easy to both read and skim?

# **Choosing A Post Topic**

- Click to the client’s most recent content interview (in your brief)  
- Read/listen through until you find something *potentially interesting*  
- When you do, ask yourself the following questions:

When you have an idea for a post from your client’s content interview, ask yourself these 3 questions. It **must** satisfy at least 1 of these 3:

1. **Will this topic make the client’s audience know them better?**

   Typically, these will be stories and posts about personal experiences.

   1. [Example 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/elirubel_i-credit-1-mentor-for-helping-me-grow-my-activity-7238909073969012737-_T_y?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Personal story that led to great outcome  
      2. [Example 2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tyler-leber_coconut-va-reached-25m-arr-in-less-than-activity-7232725779082551299-lV21?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Company origin story (also led to great oucome)  
      3. [Example 3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dennisonalajajr_i-spent-last-week-in-ohio-doing-something-activity-7237074605973069824-MkCV?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Story \+ announcement of something positive  
      4. [Example 4](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dennisonalajajr_i-started-a-phone-screen-repair-business-activity-7234537797041143808-E8YD?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Story \+ takeaway \+ relevant picture  
      5. [Example 5](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/elirubel_i-waived-150000-in-project-fees-in-exchange-activity-7237104719075143680-Vziz?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Interesting story \+ great result \+ video  
           
2. **Will this topic make the client’s audience like them better?**

   Typically, these will be opinions, pro-tips, and how-to’s.

   1. [Example 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dennisonalajajr_how-our-agency-went-from-0-15-20-high-quality-activity-7238886520521121792-lgi9?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Authority \+ promise of end result \+ process  
      2. [Example 2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tyler-leber_i-have-100-team-members-that-work-remote-activity-7237112187528388608-suTG?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Authority \+ opinion (picture helps here)  
      3. [Example 3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nick-abraham_the-4-step-sequence-is-dead-heres-how-top-activity-7236712101082189824-wMQf?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Big promise \+ authority from stats \+ tactical takeaway  
      4. [Example 4](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/elirubel_psa-youre-only-allowed-to-say-youre-doing-activity-7237821890537385985-niWs?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Hot take on controversial topic  
      5. [Example 5](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tyler-leber_we-saved-50000-of-ltv-each-month-by-sending-activity-7237839142678650881-efPC?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Quirky hook \+ behind the scenes math  
           
3. **Will this topic make the client’s audience trust them more?**

   Typically, these will be case study or social-proof-heavy posts, as well as posts where the client gets **extra** vulnerable/transparent

   1. [Example 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nick-abraham_ive-now-sent-15000000-cold-emails-for-activity-7239248857623052289-EXk8?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Lots of authority in hook \+ tactical help after  
      2. [Example 2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/orencharnoff_on-todays-episode-of-dtc-stats-that-sound-activity-7173327487018360833-FCIT?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Case study reformatted as post  
      3. [Example 3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/retentionadam_we-closed-august-24-at-234m-arr-6-activity-7237559882797703168-thhC?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Extreme transparency  
      4. [Example 4](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nick-abraham_i-spoke-with-ajay-goel-the-founder-of-gmass-activity-7234537770356981762-iSIM?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Authority take on hot topic at the time  
      5. [Example 5](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nick-abraham_how-to-build-a-high-quality-list-of-decision-makers-activity-7232725869079764992-bCv5?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Pure value his audience can implement right away.

**Notes:**

1. You’ll notice some of these topics fall into multiple buckets (like \+ trust them better, for example). That’s more than fine.  
2. Bonus if the topic is one that usually incites comments. Things people generally disagree on/have a take on. Remote work is a great example of this. We do **not** want to over-use it, but if a client has a good take on it, feel free.

### **If The Post Idea Checks Those Boxes**

1. ### Read through the client’s last few weeks of LinkedIn posts

2. ### Read through the client’s internal calendar

If the post topic has already been covered, we do not want to cover it again.

The **only** way we want to cover it again is if you come up with a new angle for the source material.

As an example:

[This post](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nick-abraham_ive-now-sent-15000000-cold-emails-for-activity-7239248857623052289-EXk8?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) shares pro tips for the client’s ICP. A way to reframe this is highlighting the opposite of each pro tip point as a mistake. Example:

---

I've sent 15,000,000 cold emails for \>250 offers. Here's what’s (unknowingly) stopping you from getting replies:

1. Things Messed Up Outside Offer  
* No VSL on landing page  
* No testimonials on landing page  
* Bad third-party reviews (G2)  
* No high-quality case studies  
* Founder inactive on social page  
* Company inactive on social

---

The post goes on, but you get the point. Note that this is a rare case. We really only do this to repurpose extremely high-performing topics.

If you have any questions at all about this, message me on Slack and I will clarify for you.

Once you have the post topic, and the clear takeaway that reader will get from reading the post, you have to write a hook that will make them read it in the first place.

# **Hook Writing 101**

The only goal of the hook is to make the reader stop scrolling and press “see more” on LinkedIn. Any word in the hook that doesn’t lend itself to that goal should be cut.

You do this by creating a *curiosity gap*: A gap between what they know, and what they’re curious to know after reading your hook.

There are a few key ways to do this. You **can** combine methods, but **do not have** to. The writing **must** sound natural when you read it out loud.

**Methods below:**

### **1a) Build Authority**

People won’t read if they have no reason to trust you. But you only have so many characters to make them trust you before they scroll on.

So, you have to build that trust in your hook. You generally do this with numbers/figures relating to **time, money, or volume**.

The idea is that because you’ve spent the time, made the money, or put the reps in some other way, you are to be trusted.

Examples of authority hooks:

- I’m the CEO of a 20-person startup. Here’s how we build culture without boring team-building activities:  
- I spent 7 years in Big 4 consulting before starting \[Company\]. Here are 4 lessons I learned that carried over:  
- I’ve sent 375,000 cold emails this week. Here are our top 3 best-performing templates:


### **1b) Use Specific Numbers**

Numbers help build authority. But, the more specific the numbers, the better.

Notice how each of the 1\) variations of hooks are *okay (and build authority),* but the 2\) variations are that much better because of how specific they are.

**We always want to write hooks like the b) variations.**

1. Last month we made 6 figures. Here’s our profit/loss:  
2. Last month we made $151,323.60. Here’s our profit/loss:  
     
1. I’ve built dozens of websites in the last 2 years. I have one pro tip for converting more visitors:  
2. I’ve built 37 websites in the last 22 months. I have one pro tip for converting more visitors:

1. I sent thousands of cold emails last month. Here are our campaign stats:  
2. I sent 10,452 cold emails last month. Here are our campaign stats:

1. I read a chapter a day for half a year. It changed my life forever. Here’s what happened:  
2. I read 1 chapter/day for 186 days. It changed my life forever. Here’s what happened:

#### **Examples**

[Example Post 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nick-abraham_ive-now-sent-15000000-cold-emails-for-activity-7239248857623052289-EXk8?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)

[Example Post 2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tyler-leber_i-have-100-team-members-that-work-remote-activity-7237112187528388608-suTG?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)

[Example Post 3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/paulblankley_we-have-5-harvard-degrees-on-our-product-activity-7239301082466652161-aDFk?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)

Notice in each of the above posts: The reader would have no reason to care about the second line if the first line wasn’t there.

---

### **2\) Start With A Story**

People love stories. Use them to your advantage to create a curiosity gap.

Read the below examples to see how stories can improve hooks.

1. Cold email is working really well for us right now.

2. Last month we tried a growth strategy I NEVER thought we’d try. It changed our business forever:

3. Here’s an answer on if you should be posting every day:

4. Yesterday, my biggest client asked me a question every Founder wants the answer to:

5. People don’t realize how valuable having a VA can be.

6. I tried using a VA for 2 weeks and I’m never going back. Here’s the story:

Notice how the Hook b) option is more engaging every time?

#### **Examples**

[Example 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/elirubel_7-years-ago-i-thought-agency-owners-were-activity-7239271507925811200-XAc1?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tyler-leber_we-saved-50000-of-ltv-each-month-by-sending-activity-7237839142678650881-efPC?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dennisonalajajr_i-can-get-it-done-for-cheaper-a-prospect-activity-7234900120310333440-lylc?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)

---

### **3\) Use : and …**

These signify that there’s more to read (thereby inciting the action of clicking “see more”).

Use these in 99% of your hooks. There are very few cases where it doesn’t make sense to use these.

Note: The sentence before the *colon* or *elipses* **must** create a curiosity gap. If it doesn’t, they are useless.

[Example 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tyler-leber_995-of-startups-get-0-in-funding-heres-activity-7234264593647218688-vRlm?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dennisonalajajr_how-our-agency-went-from-0-15-20-high-quality-activity-7238886520521121792-lgi9?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dibratto_should-your-ceo-post-about-founder-mode-activity-7237436892835684352-rrLQ?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)

---

### **4\) Highlight A Process**

Clients often share processes they use to achieve an end result. They make for great hooks/posts, but they **must** be written correctly.

If you want to highlight a process in a post:

1. Highlight the end result of the process in the hook.  
2. Use “here’s how” or “how…” somewhere in the hook to indicate the reader will learn the process by reading the post.  
3. If possible\* include the time frame and amount of steps.

Some possible **templates**:

1. \[our/my\] \[step count\] process for \[achieving end result\] in \[time frame\]

2. My 5-step process for writing 10 LinkedIn posts in 90 minutes:

3. I \[achieve end result\] in \[time frame\] using \[our/my\] \[step count\] process. Here’s how it works:

4. I write 10 LinkedIn posts in 90 minutes using my 5-step process. Here’s how it works:

5. \[I/we\] \[achieve end result\] in \[time frame\] \[without common pain point\] using \[our/my/this\] \[step count\] process

6. I write 10 LinkedIn posts in 90 minutes without ANY writers block using this 5-step proceess:

#### **Examples**

[Example 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dennisonalajajr_how-our-agency-went-from-0-15-20-high-quality-activity-7238886520521121792-lgi9?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- End result, time frame, amount of steps

[Example 2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dibratto_how-i-use-data-to-write-content-that-gets-activity-7237799250221264896-YoOQ?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- End result \+ addressing common pain point (guesswork)

[Example 3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nick-abraham_how-to-build-a-high-quality-list-of-decision-makers-activity-7232725869079764992-bCv5?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- “How to” plus big promise of desired end result

---

### **5\) Promise A Listicle**

Listicles are posts that share a specific number of points (lessons, pro tips, mistakes, etc). Whatever you’re making the listicle about **must** satisfy one of [these](https://www.notion.so/SOP-How-To-Pick-A-Post-Topic-0c148aceb8834293956983476e9f90d2?pvs=21) requirements.

**Guidelines:**

- Never promise a listicle for 2 or less points  
- Craft your listicles in odd numbers up to 10, as well as 10

3, 5, 7, 9, 10 \[things I learned, mistakes I made, pro tips, etc\]

**Do not** make listicles of 2, 4, 6, 8, or anything above 10\.

**REMEMBER:** No less than 3, no more than 10, no even numbers in between.

Listicle hooks perform best when combined with authority.

Below are examples. Notice how the 2\) variation of each hook is much more appealing?

1. 7 learnings that translate from consulting to startups:  
2. I spent 7 years in Big 4 consulting before starting \[company\]. 7 lessons I learned that I still use today:

1. 3 common cold email mistakes:  
2. I send 375,000 cold emails per week for 150+ offers. Here are 3 cold email mistakes I NEVER let my team make:

1. 9 rules for leadership CEOs should follow  
2. I’m the CEO of a 27-person remote startup. Here are 9 rules for leadership I wish I knew on Day 1:

Alternatively, you can use:

-  Desired benefits \- If you want \[desired benefit\], here are 7 \[actions\] you MUST do:  
-  Dreaded pain points \- If you want to \[avoid desired pain point\], here are 7 things you MUST avoid:

#### **Examples:**

[Example 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/paulblankley_if-you-want-to-guarantee-a-successful-career-activity-7229537499088347141-2Y3U?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- \[If you want desired benefit\], there are 3 things you need to do.

[Example 2](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7239312848898703361?updateEntityUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_updateV2%3A%28urn%3Ali%3Aactivity%3A7239312848898703361%2CFEED_DETAIL%2CEMPTY%2CDEFAULT%2Cfalse%29&lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Ad_flagship3_profile_view_base%3BLGOq5qIPRGmUuPaj9SSV0Q%3D%3D) \- Same

[Example 3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dibratto_if-i-were-a-cmo-at-an-early-stage-startup-activity-7213519234365108226-Kn6r?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) \- Notice how this doesn’t promise a listicle but instead promises a “playbook” \[sequence of steps to achieve X result\]. This only works because the graphic clearly shows a process.

---

### **6\) Make A Bold Statement**

Bold statements take on one of a few roles. You’ll notice these examples are fairly similar. That’s the point. I just want you to get used to thinking of bold statements in this sense:

1. A hot take or contrarian opinion. This would be a client’s opinion on a traditionally divisive topic. *Example:*

**Start of Hook:** *Remote work sucks.*

2. Something that goes against what people would expect the client to say. Ex: My account is all about helping Founders get leads from social media. A bold statement for me might be:  
   **Start of Hook:** *75% of Founders shouldn’t post on social.*  
   The “unexpected” part of this is most people would expect me to say EVERY Founder should post on social \- because I’m incentivized to do so.  
3. A bold stance/opinion on a less controversial topic.

This is sort of like the hot take, but isn’t used for as divisive a topic. They can be used to share a regular opinion, but must be powerful, and not “on-the-fence”

**Examples:**

**Hook:** A 5am walk is the best way to start your day.

**Notice how I didn’t\* say:** Walking at 5am *could* make you feel way better.

**Hook:** Being a Founder and a Dad is a superpower.

**Notice how I didn’t\* say:** Some people find being a Founder and a Dad awesome.

This makes it easy to stop the scroll. But there are caveats:

1. You can’t do it too often. If you do, you’ll become “the hot take person”.  
2. Whatever you say next **must** justify the hook, or else it’ll appear click-baity.

#### **Examples**

[Example 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tyler-leber_people-who-say-outsourcing-doesnt-work-activity-7232363442794364929-DEi3?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nick-abraham_this-is-the-best-video-on-cold-email-and-activity-7234175395548307456-ns6n?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/erbilyaman_i-met-with-my-mba-professor-at-500am-it-activity-7239359375637700608-27sL?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)

---

### **7\) Borrow Authority**

You can capture attention by referencing a big name or brand. **Only** do this if it’s 100% relevant to the post.

Often times, this makes for great top-of-funnel posts breaking down a bigger company or Founder’s strategy. Examples:

Examples:

→ *Ramp* is worth $7.5B. They send 25,000 cold emails/month. I got an inside look at their strategy \- 3 takeaways from it:

→ *OpenAI* is worth $150B. I studied their landing page and discovered they were using these 7 conversion hacks:

→ *Airbnb* MASTERED founder-led content. I broke down their strategy into 3 shockingly simple steps:

Notice:

1. Some of these combine the borrowed authority \+ [listicle](https://www.notion.so/SOP-How-To-Write-A-10-10-Hook-That-Makes-Readers-Click-See-More-66c602969513445b9538f0faa42972f3?pvs=21) hook. That’s intentional.  
2. The promise here is often “X \[company/person\] \[does Y thing\], and I did all the work to simplify it so you can steal it after reading this post”

Even with a great topic, takeaway(s), and hook, if the post isn’t formatted properly, it’ll never perform. That’s why you need to understand the next section.

# **LinkedIn Post Archetypes**

## **Archetype 1 \- The Claim**

1st sentence: Claim (ideally only 1 line of text long)

* Follow the Newness, Relevancy, Controversy Framework  
* Examples of what is NOT a claim:  
* “Good marketing is really important. Here’s why.” \- that’s not a new insight.  
* Or “You need to figure out how to sell. Here’s why...” \- nothing new.  
* Examples of what IS a claim:  
* “If you’re an artist, you need to become a superstar salesperson. Here’s why...” \- that’s more controversial because it’s not intuitive to the specific audience you’re addressing (artists)  
* “The VC/fundraising model is broken”  
* “If you check email more than twice a day, you’re killing your productivity”  
* “Outsourcing your content to an agency is a bad strategy.”  
* “Just because you can't measure it doesn't mean it doesn't work.”

2nd sentence: “Here are 3/4/5 reasons why” / a version of it  
Body: Listing the 3-5 reasons, use bullet points  
Last sentence: Question \- “How do you go about it?” / “What is reason number 4?” / a version of it  
Hashtags: 2-3 hashtags  
Example:  
![][image1]

## **Archetype 2 \- The Experiment**

1st sentence: Last week/Last month we tried this…. (1 line ideally)

* Example: “3 months ago, I changed my LinkedIn headline to….”  
* Example: “Last week we took the whole team to an off-site in Cape Town”

2nd sentence: “Here’s how it went:” / “Here are my results:” or version of it  
Body:

* Recounting how it went or listing the results (bullet points)  
* Why did you do this?

Last sentence: Question \- “Have you ever tried this?” / “What would you add?” / version of it  
Hashtags: 2-3 hashtags  
Example:  
![][image2]

## **Archetype 3 \- The Question**

1st sentence: Question that your prospects ask you in quotation marks (ideally 1 line)

* Example: “How do I get my first 1,000 followers on LinkedIn?”  
* Or “How do I calculate my LTV when I’m just starting out?”

2nd sentence: immediately jump into the answer OR “Here’s how:” / “Here are 3/4/5 ways to go about it:” / a version of it  
Body: Describe how to do it. If you can have a bullet list of of the 3/4/5 ways to go about it, structure it that way  
Last sentence: Question \- “How do you go about it?” / “Which method did I miss?”  
Hashtags: 2-3 hashtags  
Example:  
![][image3]

## **Archetype 4 \- The Objection**

1st sentence: A common objection your prospects often bring up (ideally 1 line)

* Example: “I don’t have the time to create content”

2nd-3rd sentence: Give a little more context/background why they say that. What’s the reason they believe this to be true?  
Body: Handle the objection. List the 1-3 reasons why they’re wrong.  
Last sentence: Bring it back to the initial objection. Example: “So if you think you don’t have the time to create content, remember….”  
Hashtags: 2-3 hashtags  
Example:  
![][image4]

## **Archetype 5 \- The Advice**

1st sentence: “Don’t … \[advice\]” OR “STOP doing….” (ideally 1 line)

* It needs to be something that your target audience is currently doing but need to stop  
* Examples:  
* “Don’t post on LinkedIn on Mondays.”  
* “Don’t run ads on Facebook for your SaaS product.”  
* “Don’t try to be nice.”

2nd sentence: “Here’s why:” OR some background from the other person’s standpoint, e.g. “People often do that because they believe….” OR some background from your standpoint “I stopped doing this last year, because…”  
Body: Describe why and/or what they need to be doing instead.  
Last sentence: Question (related to examples of 1st sentence) \- “When are you posting on LinkedIn?” / “Where are you running your ads?” / “How are you behaving differently to last year?”  
Hashtags: 2-3 hashtags

## Archetype 6 \- The Personal Story

[Ben Bradbury](https://www.linkedin.com/in/benbradbury) describes this archetype best:  
“The personal story post formula looks like this:

* Highlight a vulnerable Failure  
* Twist the knife  
* Reveal the “Aha moment”  
* Show the subsequent change  
* Leave them with an emotional connection

1\. Highlight a vulnerable Failure  
First, put yourself out there by being vulnerable. Highlight a fault or shortcoming. Negative newspaper headlines sell better than positive ones because people like controversy. It’s the same on LinkedIn. What fault or flaw can you admit in yourself that would resonate with your audience?  
2\. Twist the knife  
Second, make the problem worse. Give the audience a taste of what it’s like to have that issue at its worst possible form, which creates empathy. This is possibly the most important word you’ll need to remember: if you can create empathy, you’ll create an audience that cares about what you have to say. That’s an audience that buys.  
3\. Reveal the “Aha moment”  
Next, what was the insight that made everything better? Where did the crucial turning point occur? This is the insight that forms the basis of the post. You can often look for aha moments first when creating story posts, just think about anything that had a profound effect on you in the past. Then work backwards to figure out the other 4 steps afterwards.  
4\. Show the subsequent change  
How did the aha moment change you? What was the impact? This might be where you shared what you learned with the audience. If it’s a personal story, you might scale up the impact of the aha moment quickly (e.g. “After I learned that, I landed my first client. Then the next ten.”)  
5\. Leave them with an emotional connection  
This is crucial: Your content has to leave the audience with an emotional connection. What can you teach them from your story? Is it a way of living a better life? A tangible lesson surrounding your business niche? Whatever it is, there needs to be a connection. That’s how your audience comes back for your next piece of content. That’s how you’re remembered.”

## Archetype 7 \- The Announcement

**Tone:** Be excited and grateful. (exclamation marks are your friend here)  
1st sentence: As concisely as possible, state what the news is. Examples:

* We were featured in Forbes this week\!  
* We just moved into our new office\!  
* We hired a new COO\!

2nd sentence: Background \- why were you featured? What led to you moving into a new office? Who is this new COO?  
Body: Keep it short and to the point. Talking for too long about why you deserved to be featured in Forbes makes it too braggy.  
Last sentence: The “thank you”. Examples:

* Thanks @\[Name of Forbes writer\] for writing about us\!  
* Thanks to the team for being awesome and enabling this growth\!  
* Thanks @\[Name of COO\] for joining us\!

1-3 Hashtags

* Makes the first one relevant to the news: \#forbes \#office \#hiring etc  
* Make the remaining ones about their company: \#sales \#marketing etc

# **Post Formatting 101**

\*\*[Use this website to preview your LinkedIn post on desktop and mobile before posting](https://www.breakcold.com/tools/linkedin-post-preview-generator). 

The following two posts are the exact same. But, one is properly formatted for LinkedIn, while the other isn’t. Which version is easier to read?

**VERSION 1**

| The biggest social goldmine of 2024 is startups with \>$1,000,000,000 market cap's who's CEOs don't post. 3 things I'd tell one in Sept 2024: Anything you say is seen as gospel. Being CEO of a \>$1B startup will do that. This manifests in social metrics. Translation: For every 8-10 posts you don't write, you miss out on 1M eyeballs that could've been steered towards your company. I've seen these metrics first-hand. Your competitor(s) are doing it. For industries where multiple big players dominate, it's rare that at least one of their CEOs aren't posting.Either be the person eating your competitors' lunch, or compete with the person who currently is. You are wildly resourced. Spending $10K+/month on content is unattainable for small Founders. Not for you. You're well-positioned to make a serious investment and drive results (literally) from Day 1\. ...so if you happen to be reading this post (which oddly happens more than you'd realize), and want a content engine running in 14 days, DM me\! |
| :---- |

**VERSION 2**

| The biggest social goldmine of 2024 is startups with \>$1,000,000,000 market cap's who's CEOs don't post. 3 things I'd tell one in Sept 2024: 1\) Anything you say is seen as gospel. Being CEO of a \>$1B startup will do that. This manifests in social metrics.  Translation: For every 8-10 posts you don't write, you miss out on 1M eyeballs that could've been steered towards your company. I've seen these metrics first-hand. 2\) Your competitor(s) are doing it. For industries where multiple big players dominate, it's rare that at least one of their CEOs aren't posting. Either be the person eating your competitors' lunch, or compete with the person who currently is. 3\) You are wildly resourced. Spending $10K+/month on content is unattainable for small Founders. Not for you. You're well-positioned to make a serious investment and drive results (literally) from Day 1\. ...so if you happen to be reading this post (which oddly happens more than you'd realize), and want a content engine running in 14 days, DM me\! |
| :---- |

In case it’s not clear, the best LinkedIn posts are formatted for *skimmability.* 

**Rules of thumb to follow:**

1. **Never** have blocks of text that span more than 4 lines on the mobile view of LinkedIn.

2. Use lists and bullets to separate points and takeaways.  
      
3. **Never** use special characters (**bold**, *italics*, underlines)

# **Choosing Media For A Post**

**Please watch [this Loom](https://www.loom.com/share/1aa810cbfff34b398974f9c3208e8d82) for full context.**

Media is just as important as the copy in a lot of cases.

Choosing the right image/video can **2x results**.

Choosing the wrong image/video can **kill results**.

There are a few types of media we can choose from:

**NOTE:** You can overrule any of the below if me or the client calls for a specific image in the content interview, and/or you have a better idea specific to the post.

[This post](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tyler-leber_we-saved-50000-of-ltv-each-month-by-sending-activity-7237839142678650881-efPC?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) (read then study image) is a great example.

---

### **1\) Picture of Founder W/Face Showing**

Pictures of the Founder **where their face is showing** perform best.

These are best for posts where:

- The Founder gets [vulnerable](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dennisonalajajr_ive-been-lying-to-you-for-a-long-time-activity-7236712088520286208-tkEG?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)  
- The Founder [tells a story about a specific experience](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tyler-leber_i-have-100-team-members-that-work-remote-activity-7237112187528388608-suTG?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)  
- The Founder [**isn’t** sharing an extremely tactical process](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dennisonalajajr_how-our-agency-went-from-0-15-20-high-quality-activity-7238886520521121792-lgi9?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)  
  - See how a picture of Dennis would make 0 sense there?

Other examples of posts where pics of the Founder made most sense:

[Example 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dennisonalajajr_i-spent-last-week-in-ohio-doing-something-activity-7237074605973069824-MkCV?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/activity-7237134036052103168-p6vf?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dibratto_i-joined-the-dark-side-today-did-something-activity-7235262585183293440-h08J?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)

**To request:** Put “Picture of \[Founder name\]” in the “IMAGE:” part of the post template.

### **2\) Internal Document/Asset**

This is best for when the client describes a system, checklist, or other document that is the subject of the post.

The idea is the reader gets a “behind the scenes look” into something valuable (financials, process, etc)

[Example 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nick-abraham_15-of-our-cold-email-replies-in-the-last-activity-7226927857820655618--UDe?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dennisonalajajr_i-have-a-theory-if-im-right-ill-flood-activity-7213881607202463744-0BeV?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/elirubel_my-2-agencies-will-hit-a-24m-profit-run-activity-7239996247246315520-gMxF?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)

### **3\) Video Clip**

When there is an opportunity to use video, we use video.

If the source material you are writing from is a podcast or interview clip where the Founder is on video, **request the video.**

**To request:** Put “Need clip: \[start time\] \- \[end time\] in \[interview\]” in the “IMAGE:” part of the post template *(please hyperlink the interview)*

### **4\) Chart/Graph**

If any math or correlation between two factors is the focal point of your post, request a chart or graph.

Use your judgement—the chart/graph **must** make sense for the graphic.

[Example 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tyler-leber_1500-people-apply-to-join-our-community-activity-7236771907667148800-79iy?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dennisonalajajr_my-agencys-revenue-is-up-250-since-i-acquired-activity-7222216568686960640-pKMP?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nick-abraham_in-june-our-reply-rate-went-from-3-4-to-activity-7229464559672025089-itei?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)

**To request:** Put “Chart” OR “Graph” *and describe the chart of graph* in the “IMAGE:” part of the post template.

### **5a) Fake Tweet**

Use these when a picture of the Founder **wouldn’t** make sense, but neither would an internal document or graph, and there’s no corresponding video clip.

The idea’s that in *most* cases, it’s good to have some form of media. These are good candidates to use when nothing else makes sense.

[Example 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tyler-leber_i-sold-my-first-startup-right-after-college-activity-7232001037224550400-IgfE?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dennisonalajajr_last-week-a-new-client-asked-me-something-activity-7235262571925102593-TndP?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dibratto_how-i-use-data-to-write-content-that-gets-activity-7237799250221264896-YoOQ?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)

### **5b) Notes screenshot**

Use as an alternative to fake tweets. They serve the same purpose.

These are specifically good for highlighting a process, workflow, or listicle.

[Example 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dennisonalajajr_how-our-agency-went-from-0-15-20-high-quality-activity-7238886520521121792-lgi9?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dennisonalajajr_i-get-250-cold-emails-per-month-and-maybe-activity-7236349680308076546-QyBp?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)

**To request:** Put “Fake tweet” OR “Notes screenshot” *and the corresponding copy* in the “IMAGE:” part of the post template.

### **6\) No Media**

These are best for when nothing makes sense—including fake tweets. Use your judgement, as this is subjective.

[Example 1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/dibratto_last-week-hat-tip-had-a-new-client-love-activity-7236349746246737920-h8qa?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/tclarkmedia_if-i-wanted-to-launch-founder-led-content-activity-7239312848898703361-KqlX?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop) [Example 3](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nick-abraham_i-spoke-with-ajay-goel-the-founder-of-gmass-activity-7234537770356981762-iSIM?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop)

If you have any questions at all about this, message me on Slack and I will clarify for you.

**To request:** Put “N/A” in the “IMAGE:” part of the post template.

# **Analyzing Post Performance**

Monitor the Founders you write for’s LinkedIn profiles to see how your posts perform.

How they perform can and will inform how to write future batches of content.

Here’s how to evaluate if a post was a winner, and what to do if it wasn’t:

1. **Likes**: This one’s obvious—the more likes, the better. These are a positive signal of if your content is resonating. But that’s not all you can rely on.

2. **Quality of Likes:** This is the most important, by far. We’d rather have 20 likes from the client’s ICP vs 500 from people who aren’t. Go through the people that like clients’ posts, and see if they fit the client’s ICP. If they do, you’re in a good spot. If they don’t, we need to adjust.

3. **Comment sentiment:** This will vary post-to-post. Broadly, though, if you’re getting tons of positive comments on a post, you know you’re doing something right.
